subsections.label: A

subsections.label: B

paragraphs: i. All activities associated with Class I Industrial uses shall be enclosed within the principal structure on the lot. ii. All activities associated with On-Farm Processing shall be enclosed within a structure on the lot.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Fire and Explosion:
paragraphs: i. The manufacture of flammable liquids and gases and explosive materials is prohibited. ii. All flammable and explosive materials used in processing shall be protected by adequate safety devices against the hazard of fire and explosion, and adequate firefighting and fire suppression equipment and devices which are standard for such industry or activity.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Vibration: All industrial uses shall cause no inherent and recurring generated
paragraphs: vibration at any point along the lot line. Temporary construction and maintenance activities are excluded from this restriction.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Noise [as measured by The American National Standards Institute (ANSI)
paragraphs: Standard S1.1, Acoustical Terminology]: i. Noise shall not exceed 45 fast, A-weighted decibels (LAFmax) at or beyond the lot line of the property from which it originates from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. Specifically exempted from these standards are: a. Temporary maintenance or construction activity; b. Transportation vehicles not used in the ordinary operation of a use or a business; and c. Occasionally used safety signals, warning devices, and emergency relief valves. ii. Noise shall not exceed 40 fast, A-weighted decibels (LAFmax) at or beyond the lot line of the property from which it originates from 7:30 p.m. to 7:30 a.m. Specifically exempted from this standard are: a. Emergency repair or maintenance necessary to protect life or property; and b. Repair or maintenance conducted by the municipality; and c. Occasionally used safety signals, warning devices, and emergency relief valves; and d. Snow removal operations. iii. In no case and at no time shall noise exceed 30 fast, A-weighted decibels (LAFmax) indoors at any existing surrounding residences. subsections.label: F

paragraphs: people and are detectable at the property line are not permitted.

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Emissions, Particulates and Air Pollution:
paragraphs: i. No emissions shall be permitted which can cause any damage to health, animals, vegetation, or other forms of property, or which can cause any excessive soiling at any point on or beyond the property. ii. Dust created by an industrial operation shall not be exhausted or wasted directly into the atmosphere. iii. Dust and other types of air pollution borne by the wind from such sources as storage areas and roads shall be minimized by landscaping or other acceptable means.

subsections.label: H

paragraphs: neighboring buildings or land uses.

subsections.label: I

paragraphs: increase perceptible to humans on any humans on any adjacent property, whether such change be in air, ground or water temperature, or in the temperature of any structure adjoining the property.

subsections.label: J

subsections.label: K

subsections.label: L

paragraphs: i. Open storage of materials incidental to Class I Industrial uses is prohibited. ii. The open storage of lumber or other combustible materials shall be situated so it may be accessible to fire trucks at any time.

subsections.label: M
subsections.title: Traffic and Road Access:
paragraphs: i. Class I Industrial uses shall have no more than three (3) semi-truck deliveries per day. ii. Impervious surfaces for parking, loading, and general vehicular circulation shall cover no more than 50% of the buildable area of the lot. S 501: Statutory Authorization and Effect In accordance with 10 V.S.A. Chapter 32, and 24 V.S.A. Chapter 117 S4424, S4411, S4414, and 24 V.S.A. Chapter 59, and in accordance with the intentions specifically stated in S102 of these unified development bylaws, there is hereby established a bylaw for areas at risk of flood damage in the Town of Sutton, Vermont. Except as additionally described below, all administrative procedures follow municipal procedures described in Article IX of these bylaws. S 502: Warning of Disclaimer of Liability These regulations do not imply that land outside of the areas covered by this bylaw will be free from flood or erosion damages. These regulations shall not create liability on the part of the Town of Sutton, or any municipal official or employee thereof, for any flood or erosion damage that results from reliance on these regulations, or any administrative decision lawfully made hereunder. S 503: Lands to Which These Regulations Apply How Sutton's Flood Hazard Regulations Work The town of Sutton has opted to join the National Flood Insurance Program, which allows ALL property owners in Sutton to purchase flood insurance at more affordable rates. In order to join the National Flood Insurance Program, the Town must adopt and enforce regulations that, at a minimum, meet FEMA's standards set forth in 44 CFR. These regulations, therefore, use the technical terms in 44 CFR. Some of the more common terms are explained and illustrated here. Refer to Article XI for precise definitions. NOTE: These regulations meet the minimum standards and requirements of 44 CFR and are explained in greater detail in footnotes. Special Flood Hazard Areas are areas exposed to more than a 1 % chance of inundation by overflow from rivers and streams in any given year. (This flood event is called the "base flood" or the "100 year flood." The latter term is misleading because the flooding can occur much more frequently than once a century! The Special Flood Hazard Area is mapped by FEMA to identify risk for the National Flood Insurance Program. This area is composed of the floodway, where the waters run the deepest and fastest. The remaining portion outside of the floodway is known as the flood fringe. Sutton's FEMA maps (known as a Flood Insurance Rate Map) do not delineate the floodways. sections.title: For purposes of these regulations, the following types of planned unit development may
paragraphs: be considered:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Mixed Use PUD: Incorporates a mix of uses normally allowed in the zoning
paragraphs: district where the development is located, and is intended to maintain and reinforce traditional development patterns. Mixed use planned unit developments may or may not involve the subdivision of land, or condominium style development. They are allowed in the Village District and in the Residential District.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Conservation PUD: Clusters development to protect open space, the town's rural
paragraphs: character, and avoids the fragmentation of Sutton's working agricultural and forestry lands. Conservation planned unit developments are allowed in all districts as may be appropriate, but are specifically encouraged in the Working Lands District and the Rural District.

sections.title: To encourage integrated master planning, a planned unit development may incorporate
paragraphs: multiple adjoining properties in common ownership, or in separate ownership if a joint PUD application is filed by all participating property owners. One contact person shall be identified on a joint application to coordinate development review proceedings with all participating property owners and to facilitate communications with the Town. S 803: Application Requirements

sections.title: In addition to the submittal requirements normally required under Article VII or S 208
paragraphs: of these regulations, an application for Planned Unit Development shall contain a master plan of the proposed development, legibly drawn to scale on sheets of no more than 24" by 36" outside measurement, depicting the following:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Property and lot boundaries;

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Location, height, and spacing of existing and proposed structures at buildout;

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The location, extent and intended use of designated open spaces areas;

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Streets, driveways and off-street parking, unloading and service area;

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Utility lines, storm and natural drainage, and septic systems;

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Proposed lighting; and

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Such other features as the Development Review Board may require, such as areas
paragraphs: set aside for agriculture or forestry uses.

sections.title: The application shall also be accompanied by a narrative statement that includes the
paragraphs: following:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: The nature of all proposed modifications, changes, or supplements to the existing
paragraphs: regulations, including, but not limited to increases in the allowed density of development and requested changes to district dimensional standards. Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 53

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Overall level or intensity of development at buildout, including the maximum
paragraphs: number of households, residents, or occupants, trip generation rates, and the maximum design capacity of buildings and infrastructure.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: A schedule for the phasing of development in relation to the available capacity of
paragraphs: existing and planned infrastructure and facilities intended to serve the proposed development.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: For projects that include affordable or senior housing, associated administrative

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Proposed measures to mitigate or offset adverse impact of concentrated higher

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Evidence of established and proposed ownership patterns and interests in the

sections.title: The proposed planned unit development shall concentrate or cluster development on the
paragraphs: most physically developable portion of the lot(s) in conformance with these regulations; and excludes from development areas of very steep slope of 25% or more, flood hazard areas, surface waters, wetlands and associated buffers.

sections.title: The proposed planned unit development shall not eliminate existing eligibility for
paragraphs: enrollment in tax abatement programs, such as Vermont Current Use program.

sections.title: The proposal shall be an effective and uniform treatment of the development
paragraphs: possibilities of the project site, including common ingress and egress on and off public roads whenever practicable. The proposed development plan shall make appropriate provision for the preservation and stabilization of flood hazard areas, streams and stream banks, steep slopes, wet areas, soils unsuitable for development, forested areas, agricultural lands, and unique, natural and man-made features.

sections.title: Common ingress and egress on and off public roads shall by accessible by dry land,
paragraphs: outside of flood hazard areas as defined in Article V of these regulations.

sections.title: The proposal shall be consistent with the Sutton Town Plan and all applicable bylaws
Mixed uses shall be arranged to be compatible and to insure visual and aural privacy for
paragraphs: residents of the project.

sections.title: The development plan may be phased over a reasonable period of time in order that
paragraphs: adequate facilities services, and infrastructure may be provided.

sections.title: Uses shall be limited to those permitted and conditional uses allowed within the
paragraphs: district(s) in which the PUD is proposed.

sections.title: Density may vary within the PUD, but the overall density shall not exceed what would
paragraphs: be permitted, if the land were developed in conformance with the zoning regulations for Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 54 the district(s) in which the PUD is proposed, unless density bonuses are granted in accordance with S 807 of these regulations. Calculation of the allowed overall density of development shall be based on total parcel(s) acreage, excluding existing and proposed road rights-of-way, and lot size and density requirements for the zoning district(s) in which the development is located. Accessory dwelling units shall not be included in density calculations.

sections.title: The Development Review Board may allow for a greater concentration of density or
paragraphs: intensity of residential land use, within some section(s) of the development than upon others, which shall be offset by a lesser concentration in any other section.

sections.title: Non-contiguous PUD: Planned unit development may be established on non-contiguous
paragraphs: lots using density averaging calculated in accordance with 804.09.

sections.title: PUD in two or more zoning districts: If the planned unit development involves two or
paragraphs: more zoning districts, the allowed overall density of development shall be the sum of the allowed density for each area of the planned unit within a particular zoning district, using the density and dimensional standards of that district. Density shall then be transferred from those areas within the lower density districts to developable portions within the higher density zoning districts.

sections.title: Roadways, parking and unloading facilities shall be designed and constructed so as not
paragraphs: to cause unreasonable highway congestion or unsafe traffic conditions. Where possible, no roadway shall have a grade at any point in excess of 10 percent.

sections.title: Signs not attached to buildings shall be consolidated in one location on the property,
paragraphs: and be of uniform size, shape, and design. Signs attached to buildings shall be of comparable design with the consolidated signs.

sections.title: The outdoor storage of raw materials or inventory shall be screened or hidden from
paragraphs: public highway view, or the view of persons in residential districts.

sections.title: Any central or community sewage disposal and water supply systems shall comply with
paragraphs: all applicable State regulations. Final approval of PUD shall be conditioned on demonstrated compliance with said regulations.

sections.title: The proposal shall provide for the preservation of open space. Open space shall be in a
paragraphs: location or locations, size, and shape approved by the Development Review Board and shall be sited and preserved in accordance with S 805 of these regulations.

sections.title: Performance Bond: The Development Review Board may require from the applicant,
paragraphs: for the benefit of the Town, a performance bond in an amount sufficient to cover the full cost of constructing any public improvements that the Development Review Board may require in approving the project, such performance bond to be submitted prior to commencement of the approved plan. S 805: Open Space Standards

sections.title: All planned unit development shall incorporate designed open space areas, as depicted
paragraphs: on the site plan or subdivision plat, that are appropriate to the type, location, and purpose of the planned development. Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 55

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Mixed Used Open Space: May include one or more common greens, playgrounds,
paragraphs: pocket parks, community gardens or other more formal open space areas for use by the residents or the general public. At minimum of 15% of the gross area of a Mixed Use PUD shall be reserved as designated open space.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Conservation Open Space: A minimum of 50% of a Conservation PUD shall be
paragraphs: reserved as designated open space. To the extent physically feasible, designated open space shall be contiguous with and functionally connected to adjacent undeveloped open space or conserved areas to limit the fragmentation of conserved resources. A Conservation PUD shall not eliminate eligibility for enrollment in tax abatement programs, such as the Vermont Current Use program.

sections.title: Designated open space shall be of a character, size, extent, and shape suitable for its
paragraphs: intended purpose or use. Designated open space areas shall not include building lots, road rights-of-way, access, or parking areas.

sections.title: Designated open space may be held in common or single ownership to include:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Ownership by nonprofit community association, corporation, legal partnership, or
paragraphs: cooperative organized under the laws of Vermont that is responsible for the maintenance of all open space, as well as roadways, and other common elements of the development.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Dedication of designated open space through conveyance of land or interests in
paragraphs: land, to a public or nonprofit entity acceptable to the Development Review Board, such as the Town of Sutton, a state or federal agency, or a land trust.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Subdivision plat or deed restriction or other legal means as approved by the
paragraphs: Development Review Board recorded in the Town of Sutton Land Records. Such restrictions shall specify that no further subdivision or development may occur; and may contain suitable "right to farm" or "right to forest" language in order to alert nearby owners about present or future forestry or agricultural operations.

sections.title: Designated open space shall be managed by the owner for its intended purpose and use,
paragraphs: as approved by the Development Review Board. The Board may require the submission of a long-term management plan for the protection and sustainable management of conserved resources.

sections.title: No future development of designated open space shall be allowed except as incidental
paragraphs: to its intended use. S 806: Density Bonuses

sections.title: The Development Review Board, at the request of the applicant, may grant one or more
paragraphs: density bonuses. These bonuses shall not increase the overall density as determined according to the standards in S 804 by more than 100 percent.

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: A density bonus of up to 50% may be considered for planned unit development
paragraphs: that meets the definition of affordable housing development as defined in Article XI in these regulations, or determined from current federal housing and income data, for at least 15 years from the date of construction. subsections.label: B
subsections.title: A density bonus of up to 50% may be considered for planned unit development
paragraphs: that meets the definition of senior housing development as defined in Article XI in these regulations, or determined from current federal housing and income data, for at least 15 years from the date of construction.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: A density bonus of up to 50% may be considered for Conservation PUD that
paragraphs: incorporates open space designated under S 806 of these regulations of at least 60% of the lot(s) in areas outside of the Working Lands District and 80% of the lot(s) in the Working Lands District.

sections.title: In order for the Development Review Board to grant one or more density bonuses, the

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Clearly document that the developable portion of the lot(s) and supporting roads,
paragraphs: infrastructure, utilities and services can accommodate higher densities of development; and

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Incorporates measures in development design necessary to mitigate adverse

sections.title: No land development, as defined in 24 VSA, S 4303(10) of the Act, may be commenced
paragraphs: without a permit issued by the Zoning Administrator. No zoning permit may be issued by the Zoning Administrator except in conformance with these regulations.

sections.title: Applications for zoning permits shall be made to the Zoning Administrator on forms
paragraphs: provided for that purpose.

sections.title: Prior to the issuance of any zoning permit the Zoning Administrator shall first satisfy
paragraphs: himself that the subject of the application is in conformance with these regulations. He may enter upon the land or premises of an applicant and may request from an applicant any information he deems necessary for this purpose. No such permit shall be issued unless an application, fee, plot plan and any other approvals of the Development Review Board required by this bylaw have been properly obtained and are submitted in connection with the application. The Zoning Administrator shall, within 30 days of submission of a complete application, data and approvals, either issue or deny a zoning Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 57 permit. If denied, the Zoning Administrator shall so notify the applicant in writing, stating his reasons therefore. If a zoning permit is issued, all activities authorized by its issuance shall be completed within two years of its date of issue, or the zoning permit shall be null and void and reapplication to undertake any activities shall be required.

sections.title: In the issuance of zoning permits, the Zoning Administrator shall comply with all of the
paragraphs: provisions of 24 VSA, S 4449.

sections.title: The fee for a zoning permit shall be established by the Legislative Body. It may be a
paragraphs: sliding scale depending on the cost of the land development. Said fee shall accompany each application for a permit.

sections.title: No zoning permit issued pursuant to 24 VSA, S 4449 shall take effect until the time for
paragraphs: Appeal in 24 VSA, S 4465(a) has passed, or in the event that a notice of appeal is properly filed, such permit shall not take effect until final adjudication of said appeal.

sections.title: No zoning permit shall be necessary for any structure that is 100 square feet or smaller
paragraphs: that is not located on a permanent foundation, provided the structure is located outside of flood hazard areas as defined in Article V of these regulations. S 903: Penalties Any violation of these regulations after the effective date thereof shall be subject to penalties as provided in 24 VSA, SS 4451 and 4452 . S 904: Development Review Board

sections.title: The Development Review Board shall consist of not fewer than five (5) nor more than
paragraphs: nine (9) members appointed by the Selectboard for specified terms in accordance with 24 V.S.A. [S4460(b) and (c)]. The Selectboard also may appoint alternates, for specified terms, to serve on the Development Review Board in situations when one or more members of the Board are disqualified or are otherwise unable to serve. Any member of the Development Review Board may be removed for cause by the Selectboard upon written charges and after public hearing.

sections.title: The Development Review Board may employ or contract for clerks, secretaries, legal
paragraphs: counsel, consultants and other technical and clerical services. All members of the board may be compensated for the performance of their duties, and may be reimbursed by the municipality for necessary and reasonable expenses.

sections.title: The Development Review Board shall adopt rules of procedure and rules of ethics with
paragraphs: respect to conflicts of interest to guide its official conduct, as required under 24 V.S.A. S4461(a) and Vermont's Open Meeting Law.

sections.title: The Development Review Board shall have all powers and duties as set forth in 24
paragraphs: V.S.A. Chapter 117 to administer the provisions of these regulations, including but not limited to the power to hear and act upon:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Appeals from any decision, act, or failure to act by the Zoning Administrator, as
paragraphs: described in S 907 of these regulations and any associated variance requests, as described in S 908 of these regulations; Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 58

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Applications for site plan approval, as described in S 207 of these regulations;

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Applications for conditional use approval, as described in S 208 these regulations;

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Applications for rights-of-way or easements for development lacking frontage, as

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Applications for subdivision approval, as described in Article 7 of this bylaw;

subsections.title: Applications for conditional uses with flood hazard areas, as described in Article
paragraphs: 5 of this bylaw; and

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Applications for planned unit developments, as described in Article 8 of this
paragraphs: bylaw. S 905: Public Notice Any public notice for a warned public hearing shall be given not less than 15 days prior to the date of the public hearing by all the following:

sections.title: Publication of the date, place, and purpose of the hearing in a newspaper of general
paragraphs: circulation in the municipality affected.

sections.title: Posting of the same information in three or more public places within the municipality
paragraphs: in conformance with location requirements of 1 VSA S 312(c) (2), including posting within view from the public right-of-way most nearly adjacent to the property for which an application is made. Posting in view from the right-of-way shall be clearly visible from all public approaches. Said posting will be done by the Zoning Administrator.

sections.title: Written notification to the applicant and to owners of all properties adjoining the
paragraphs: property subject to development, without regard to any public right-of-way. The notification shall include a description of the proposed project and shall be accompanied by information that clearly informs the recipient where additional information may be obtained, and that participation in the local proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal.

sections.title: When notification of abutting property owners is required by S 905.03, such notice shall
paragraphs: be the responsibility of the applicant and the applicant shall submit proof of such notification to the Development Review Board. The applicant shall provide acceptable proof of notification, which shall include return receipt cards, a signed affidavit from each abutting property owner indicating that they received the required notice, or if the abutter refuses notice, proof of mail delivery to the abutter's last known mailing address accompanied by sworn certificate of service. S 906: Decisions of the Development Review Board

sections.title: In accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4464(b), the Development Review Board shall issue all
paragraphs: decisions within 45 days after the adjournment of the hearing. Failure to issue a decision within the 45-day period shall be deemed approval and shall be effective the 46th day. Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 59

sections.title: All decisions shall be issued in writing and shall separately state findings of fact and
paragraphs: conclusions of law. Findings of fact shall explicitly and concisely restate the underlying facts that support the decision, based exclusively on evidence of the record. Conclusions shall be based on findings of fact. The decision shall also include a statement of the time within which appeals may be taken. The minutes of a meeting may suffice, provided that the factual basis and conclusions relating to the review standards are provided in accordance with these requirements.

sections.title: In rendering a decision in favor of the applicant, the Development Review Board may
paragraphs: attach additional reasonable conditions and safeguards as it deems necessary to implement these regulations and the town plan currently in effect.

sections.title: All decisions shall be sent by certified mail, within the required 45-day period, to the
paragraphs: applicant or the appellant on matters of appeal. Copies of the decision also shall be mailed to every person appearing and having been heard at the hearing, and filed with the Zoning Administrator and Clerk as part of the public record of the municipality. S 907: Appeals

sections.title: Appeals of decisions made by the Zoning Administrator may be made in the following
paragraphs: manner:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: An interested person, as defined in 24 VSA, S 4465, may appeal any decision or
paragraphs: act taken by the Zoning Administrator in any municipality by filing a notice of appeal with the secretary of the Sutton Development Review Board or with the Sutton Town Clerk if no such secretary has been elected. This notice of appeal must be filed within 15 days of the date of that decision or act, and a copy of the notice of appeal shall be filed with the Zoning Administrator.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: A notice of appeal shall be in writing and shall include the name and address of
paragraphs: the appellant, a brief description of the property with respect to which the appeal is taken, a reference to the regulatory provisions applicable to that appeal, the relief requested by the appellant, and the alleged grounds why the requested relief is believed proper under the circumstances.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The Sutton Development Review Board shall set a date and place for a public
paragraphs: hearing of an appeal that shall be within 60 days of the filing of the notice of appeal. The Sutton Development Review Board shall give public notice of the hearing and shall mail to the appellant a copy of that notice at least 15 days prior to the hearing date. Any person or body empowered by 24 VSA, S 4465 to take an appeal with respect to the property at issue may appear and be heard in person or be represented by an agent or attorney at the hearing. Any hearing held under this section may be adjourned by the Sutton Development Review Board from time to time; provided, however, that the date and place of the adjourned hearing shall be announced at the hearing. All hearings under this section shall be open to the public and the rules of evidence applicable at these hearings shall be the same as the rules of evidence applicable in contested cases in hearings before administrative agencies as set forth in 3 VSA S 810. Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 60

sections.title: Appeals of decisions made by the Development Review Board may be made in the
paragraphs: following manner:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: An interested person who has participated in a public hearing held in the Town of
paragraphs: Sutton with regard to an application for a permit authorized under this bylaw may appeal a decision rendered by Development Review Board to the Environmental Court. Participation in such a public hearing shall consist of offering, through oral or written testimony, evidence or a statement of concern related to the subject of the hearing. An appeal from a decision of the Development Review Board shall be taken in such manner as the Supreme Court may by rule provide for appeals from state agencies governed by 3 VSA, SS 801 through 816.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Notice of the appeal shall be filed by certified mail, with fees, to the
paragraphs: Environmental Court and by mailing a copy to the municipal clerk or the Zoning Administrator, if so designated, who shall supply a list of interested persons to the appellant within five working days. Upon receipt of the list of interested persons, the appellant shall, by certified mail, provide a copy of the notice of appeal to every interested person, and, if any one or more of those persons are not then parties to the appeal, upon motion they shall be granted leave by the Court to intervene. S 908: Variances The Development Review Board shall hear and decide requests for variances in accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4469(a) and appeal procedures under S 907 of these regulations. In granting a variance, the Development Review Board may impose conditions it deems necessary and appropriate under the circumstances to implement the purposes of these regulations and the Town Plan currently in effect. The Development Review Board may grant a variance and render a decision in favor of the appellant only if all of the following facts are found, and the findings are specified in its written decision:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: There are unique physical circumstances or conditions, including irregularity,
paragraphs: narrowness, or shallowness of lot size or shape, or exceptional topography or other physical conditions peculiar to the particular property, and the unnecessary hardship is due to the conditions and not the circumstances or conditions generally created by the provisions of these regulations in the neighborhood or district in which the property is located;

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Because of these physical circumstances or conditions, there is no possibility that the
paragraphs: property can be developed in strict conformity with the provisions of these regulations and that the authorization of a variance is necessary to enable the reasonable use of the property;

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The unnecessary hardship has not been created by the appellant;

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: The variance, if authorized, will not alter the essential character of the neighborhood or
paragraphs: district in which the property is located, substantially or permanently impair the appropriate use or development of adjacent property, reduce access to renewable energy resources, or be detrimental to the public welfare; and Unified Development Bylaw Sutton Unified Development Bylaw: Amended 4/26/28 Page 61

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: The variance, if authorized, will represent the minimum that will afford relief and will
paragraphs: represent the least deviation possible from these regulations and from the plan.

sections.title: In their interpretation and application, the provisions of these regulations shall be held
paragraphs: to be minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, comfort, convenience, and general welfare.

sections.title: It is not the intent of these regulations to repeal, annul or in any way to impair any
paragraphs: regulations or permits previously adopted or issued, provided, however, that where these regulations impose a greater restriction upon the use of a structure or land than are required by any other statute, ordinance, rule, regulation permit, easement, or agreement, the provision of these regulations shall control. S 1003: Effective Date This bylaw shall take effect 21 days after adoption in accordance with the procedures set forth in 24 VSA, SS 4441 and 4442. S 1004: Separability The invalidity of any article or section of these regulations shall not invalidate any other article or section thereof. S 1005: Repeal Upon the date of adoption of this bylaw, the former Town of Sutton Zoning Bylaw, adopted March 2, 1976, revised January 7, 1992, and further revised August 23, 2005 is hereby declared repealed and shall have no further force or effect.
